terms.gloss: A short-sleeve pullover with a plain round neckline and no collar or buttons.
terms.quickRead: A plain crew-neck T-shirt.
terms.closerRead: Everything that separates one from another is quiet: how tight and springy the ribbed collar is, the weight and hand of the cotton, and whether the shoulder seam sits right at the edge (set-in) or runs on a diagonal (raglan).
terms.plateHint: A flat T-shirt with call-outs to the ribbed neckline, the shoulder seam, and the hem finish.

terms.gloss: A collarless pullover with a short buttoned placket at the neck.
terms.quickRead: A collarless tee with a few buttons at the throat.
terms.closerRead: The short two-to-four-button placket where a collar would be is the tell; it often comes in a waffle or thermal knit that reads a little more rugged than a plain tee.
terms.plateHint: A flat pullover top with an arrow to the short buttoned neck placket and a zoom on the waffle-knit texture.

terms.gloss: A collared short-sleeve knit shirt that pulls over the head with a two- or three-button placket.
terms.quickRead: A collared short-sleeve shirt that pulls over the head.
terms.closerRead: The soft folded collar, the short button placket, and the waffle-textured piqué knit are the tells; the back hem that dips lower than the front is the 'tennis tail,' meant to stay tucked.
terms.plateHint: A flat polo showing the ribbed collar, the two-button placket, and the longer curved back hem labeled 'tennis tail.'

terms.gloss: A soft, warm button-up made from brushed cotton, most often in a plaid pattern.
terms.quickRead: A soft, warm plaid button-up shirt.
terms.closerRead: 'Flannel' actually names the brushed, fuzzy cloth, not the plaid people usually mean; run a hand across it and you feel the raised nap that traps warmth.
terms.plateHint: A flat button-up shirt with a zoom-in swatch of the brushed napped weave, labeled to separate the cloth from the plaid pattern.

terms.gloss: A round-neck pullover made of looped-back fleece with ribbed neck, cuffs, and hem.
terms.quickRead: A plain round-neck sweatshirt.
terms.closerRead: The ribbed neck, cuffs, and hem, plus the small V-stitch or triangle gusset at the collar, are the tells; inside is looped-back fleece, and it’s simply the hood-less cousin of the hoodie.
terms.plateHint: A flat sweatshirt with call-outs to the ribbing and the V-gusset at the collar, plus a cutaway of the loopback fleece interior.

terms.gloss: A hooded fleece sweatshirt, usually with a drawstring hood and a front hand-pocket.
terms.quickRead: A hooded sweatshirt with a front pocket.
terms.closerRead: Drawstring hood, kangaroo hand-pocket, and ribbed cuffs and hem; the fleece weight and whether the hood is double-lined enough to stand up are what separate a substantial one from a thin one.
terms.plateHint: A flat hoodie with arrows to the drawstring hood, the kangaroo pocket, and the ribbed cuff and hem.

terms.handle: the denim shirt that isn’t denim
terms.gloss: A lightweight cotton button-up woven from a colored warp and a white weft, giving a soft faded-blue look.
terms.quickRead: A soft blue button-up work shirt.
terms.closerRead: It reads like denim but wears far lighter and smoother; the plain over-under weave (not denim’s diagonal twill) is the tell, and up close you see white threads flickering through the blue.
terms.plateHint: A flat button-up shirt with a zoom-in swatch of the plain colored-warp/white-weft weave, set beside a denim twill swatch.

terms.gloss: A heavy knit sport shirt with a contrasting hard collar, bold horizontal stripes, and reinforced buttons.
terms.quickRead: A striped, collared long-sleeve sport shirt.
terms.closerRead: Heavier than a polo, with a hard-wearing white twill collar, bold horizontal hoops, and short rubber buttons built not to crack in a scrum; every detail traces back to the field.
terms.plateHint: A flat rugby shirt with call-outs to the contrast twill collar, the reinforced rubber buttons, and the horizontal hoop stripes.

terms.gloss: A polo made from a looser, sweater-like knit rather than a springy piqué.
terms.quickRead: A polo made of a softer, sweater-like knit.
terms.closerRead: Instead of the athletic piqué, the whole shirt is knitted like a fine sweater; the open, textured knit and often a flat camp-style collar give it a retro, resort feel.
terms.plateHint: A flat polo with a zoom on the open sweater-knit stitch, contrasted with a piqué waffle swatch.

terms.gloss: A crisp cotton button-up made from oxford cloth, a basket-weave with a bit of body.
terms.quickRead: A crisp cotton button-up shirt.
terms.closerRead: Oxford cloth pairs two fine threads against a thicker one in a basket-weave, giving a subtle two-tone texture and a little structure you can feel; it is the workhorse button-up worn with everything.
terms.plateHint: A flat button-up shirt with a large zoom of the basket-weave oxford cloth showing the paired warp threads.

terms.gloss: A collar whose points sit fairly close together and angle downward.
terms.quickRead: A standard shirt collar.
terms.closerRead: The points sit close together and angle down toward the chest; it is the default dress-shirt collar and frames a tie in a narrow triangle.
terms.plateHint: A shirt collar shown flat with the point spread angle marked, beside a wider spread collar for comparison.

terms.gloss: A collar with the points set wide apart, leaving a broad gap at the throat.
terms.quickRead: A collar with the points set wide apart.
terms.closerRead: The points open out toward the shoulders, so there is a wide gap at the throat; it makes room for a fuller tie knot and reads a touch dressier than a point collar.
terms.plateHint: A shirt collar shown flat with the wide angle between the points marked and the throat gap highlighted.

terms.gloss: A collar whose points fasten to the shirt body with small buttons.
terms.quickRead: A collar whose points button down.
terms.closerRead: Two little buttons pin the points to the shirt so the collar keeps a soft rolling arch instead of lying flat; it started as a way to stop polo players' collars flapping, which is why it reads casual and sporty.
terms.plateHint: An open shirt collar shown flat with arrows to the two collar-point buttons and the soft roll they create.

terms.gloss: A short standing band around the neck with nothing to fold down.
terms.quickRead: A low standing collar with no fold.
terms.closerRead: Just a short upright band with no folded leaf and no lapel notch; also called a grandad or mandarin collar, it leaves the throat clean and unstructured.
terms.plateHint: A shirt neckline shown flat with the short standing band highlighted and a note that no fold-down leaf is present.

terms.gloss: A soft, open collar with no button at the throat that lies flat in a notched V.
terms.quickRead: An open, relaxed collar on a short-sleeve shirt.
terms.closerRead: There is no top button and no stand; the collar simply folds flat and often forms a little loop-and-notch at the front, and that throat-open lay is the tell of a camp shirt.
terms.plateHint: A shirt front shown flat with an arrow to the notched flat-lying collar and the absent throat button, beside a standing point collar.

terms.gloss: A collar whose points are cut into soft rounds instead of sharp tips.
terms.quickRead: A collar with rounded tips instead of pointed ones.
terms.closerRead: The points are trimmed into gentle rounds; a slightly vintage look tracing back to Eton, it is the giveaway detail that makes an otherwise plain shirt feel deliberate.
terms.plateHint: A shirt collar shown flat with the rounded point shape emphasized, beside a squared point collar for contrast.

terms.gloss: A close cut that follows the body with little extra cloth.
terms.quickRead: A close-cut, trim fit.
terms.closerRead: Trimmed through the chest, waist, and leg so it traces the body; the tell is a clean line with no drape or billow to the fabric.
terms.plateHint: A trouser-and-shirt silhouette pair with the slim outline shown against a dotted straight-fit outline for scale.

terms.gloss: A cut that runs the same width from the top down, with no taper or flare.
terms.quickRead: A fit that hangs straight down.
terms.closerRead: The leg or body stays the same width from the hip to the hem, with no narrowing and no flare; the balanced middle cut that neither hugs nor drapes.
terms.plateHint: A trouser silhouette with vertical guide lines showing equal width from hip to hem.

terms.gloss: A roomy cut with extra ease through the body so cloth drapes rather than follows.
terms.quickRead: A loose, roomy fit.
terms.closerRead: Cut with extra room through the body, seat, and thigh so the cloth falls away from you rather than tracing the body; comfort and movement are the point.
terms.plateHint: A trouser silhouette with generous ease shown as space between a body outline and the fabric line.

terms.gloss: A cut that is roomier up top and narrows gradually toward the ankle or cuff.
terms.quickRead: A fit that narrows toward the bottom.
terms.closerRead: Roomier through the top and slimming steadily toward the ankle; 'tapered' names the narrowing itself, so it can sit on top of a slim, straight, or relaxed cut.
terms.plateHint: A trouser silhouette with the outline drawn wider at the hip and converging toward a narrower ankle.

terms.gloss: A length that deliberately stops short, higher than the usual hem.
terms.quickRead: A length that stops short, above where you’d expect.
terms.closerRead: The hem ends higher on purpose, above the ankle on trousers or above the hip on a jacket, showing sock or skin; that clean high stop is the tell.
terms.plateHint: A trouser leg shown ending above the ankle bone with the exposed gap to the shoe labeled.

terms.handle: where the hem meets the shoe
terms.gloss: The amount of fabric-fold a trouser leg makes where it rests on the shoe.
terms.quickRead: How long the pants sit: whether they pool, touch, or stop above the shoe.
terms.closerRead: Full break stacks a fold or two of cloth on the shoe, half break just kisses it, and no break stops clean above; reading the break tells you how carefully a whole outfit was calibrated.
terms.plateHint: Three trouser hems side by side over the same shoe (full break, half break, no break), each labeled.

terms.gloss: A cotton-twill trouser with a smooth pleatless front.
terms.quickRead: Plain cotton trousers with a smooth front.
terms.closerRead: No pleats below the waistband, so the front lies flat; the cotton twill, that fine diagonal rib, is what makes it a chino rather than a dress trouser.
terms.plateHint: A flat trouser front with the smooth pleatless waist marked and a zoom on the diagonal twill weave.

terms.gloss: A trouser with one or two folds sewn in at the waistband for extra room.
terms.quickRead: Trousers with folds at the waistband.
terms.closerRead: One or two pleats open below the waistband to add room through the hip and thigh, then release into a cleaner drape; whether the fold points toward or away from the fly is the detail to clock.
terms.plateHint: A flat trouser front with the pleat folds at the waistband highlighted and their direction arrowed.

terms.gloss: The standard blue jean, with two front, two back, and one coin pocket.
terms.quickRead: A regular pair of blue jeans.
terms.closerRead: The five-pocket layout (two back, two front, plus the little coin pocket) with rivets at the stress points and a felled inseam is the template nearly every jean copies.
terms.plateHint: A flat pair of jeans with each of the five pockets and the rivets numbered and labeled.

terms.gloss: A trouser cut broad through the whole leg so it drapes straight and full.
terms.quickRead: Trousers cut wide all the way down.
terms.closerRead: Generous from the hip through the hem so the leg column stays broad and falls straight; a deliberate move away from the slim default.
terms.plateHint: A trouser silhouette with the wide, near-parallel leg lines shown against a dotted slim outline.

terms.gloss: A trouser with a roomy seat and thigh that collapses to a narrow, often cropped ankle.
terms.quickRead: Trousers that are roomy up top and snug at the ankle.
terms.closerRead: Pronounced room through the seat and thigh gathering into a narrow, often cropped ankle; the exaggerated carrot shape reads more dramatic than a gentle taper.
terms.plateHint: A trouser silhouette exaggerating the full hip and thigh narrowing sharply to a tight ankle.

terms.gloss: A utility trouser with large patch pockets on the thighs.
terms.quickRead: Trousers with big pockets on the legs.
terms.closerRead: Bellowed patch pockets on the thighs, often flapped, are the whole point; they add visual bulk and a clear workwear-utility read.
terms.plateHint: A flat trouser leg with the bellows thigh pocket and its flap and stitching emphasized.

terms.gloss: A soft trouser closed with a tie or elastic waistband instead of a fly and button.
terms.quickRead: Soft trousers with a tie or elastic waist.
terms.closerRead: No fly-and-button closure; a drawstring or elastic waistband does the work, so they pull on like sweatpants even when they are cut and tailored like trousers.
terms.plateHint: A flat trouser waistband with the drawcord and its exit eyelets highlighted.

terms.gloss: A straight-leg jean woven on old shuttle looms so the fabric’s own edge finishes the seam.
terms.quickRead: A straight pair of jeans.
terms.closerRead: Cuff them and you find the 'self-edge': a tight, often red-lined band woven on narrow shuttle looms so the fabric edge won’t fray; that clean selvedge line is the denim-lover’s tell.
terms.plateHint: A cuffed jean hem with a zoom on the selvedge band and its colored line along the outseam.

terms.gloss: The classic blue-jean jacket, with chest pockets and a fitted waist.
terms.quickRead: A classic blue-jean jacket.
terms.closerRead: The pointed chest-pocket flaps, the vertical waist-adjuster tabs, and the V-shaped seams down the front mark the 'Type III' trucker that every denim jacket descends from.
terms.plateHint: A flat denim jacket with call-outs to the chest pocket flaps, the waist tabs, and the front V-seams.

terms.gloss: A boxy button-up work jacket in sturdy cotton with flat patch pockets.
terms.quickRead: A boxy button-up work jacket.
terms.closerRead: Three or four flat patch pockets, a straight boxy cut, and a hard-wearing cotton or moleskin; the French 'bleu de travail' workman’s coat, worn as a light layer.
terms.plateHint: A flat boxy jacket with the patch pockets and button front labeled and the straight side seams marked.

terms.gloss: A short zip jacket with ribbed collar, cuffs, and waist, based on the military flight jacket.
terms.quickRead: A short zip-up jacket with ribbed cuffs and hem.
terms.closerRead: Ribbed knit at the collar, cuffs, and waist, a smooth front zip, and often a small zippered utility pocket on the left sleeve; the flight-jacket blueprint.
terms.plateHint: A flat bomber with the ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem and the sleeve utility pocket highlighted.

terms.gloss: A military utility jacket with four flap pockets, a drawcord waist, and a hood-hiding stand collar.
terms.quickRead: A military-style utility jacket with four front pockets.
terms.closerRead: Four bellows pockets, a drawcord waist, epaulets, and a stand collar hiding a zip-away hood; the U.S. M-65 field jacket, usually in olive drab.
terms.plateHint: A flat field jacket with the four flap pockets, the waist drawcord, and the zip-collar hood compartment labeled.

terms.gloss: A short, trim zip blouson with a stand collar and a tartan lining.
terms.quickRead: A lightweight zip-up jacket with a short collar.
terms.closerRead: A trim, hip-length zip blouson with a stand collar and elastic waist; the giveaway is the bright tartan lining and the umbrella-vent yoke across the back.
terms.plateHint: A flat harrington shown half-open to reveal the tartan lining, with the stand collar and elastic hem labeled.

terms.gloss: A long, insulated hooded coat built for cold weather.
terms.quickRead: A long, warm hooded coat.
terms.closerRead: Longer than a jacket, with an insulated body and a large hood, often fur-trimmed; the fishtail split at the back hem and the deep snorkel hood are the cold-weather tells.
terms.plateHint: A flat long parka with the hood, the insulated body quilting, and the fishtail back hem labeled.

terms.gloss: A short, heavy double-breasted wool coat of naval origin.
terms.quickRead: A short, heavy double-breasted wool coat.
terms.closerRead: Broad notched lapels, two rows of anchor-stamped buttons, and slash hand-warmer pockets in thick navy melton wool; the sailor’s coat.
terms.plateHint: A flat double-breasted coat with the two button rows, the wide lapels, and the slash pockets labeled.

terms.gloss: A heavy shirt cut and buttoned like a shirt but worn as a light jacket.
terms.quickRead: A thick shirt worn like a light jacket.
terms.closerRead: Cut and buttoned like a shirt but in a heavier cloth with a boxier body and patch pockets, warm enough to layer over a tee; the blurry line between shirt and jacket is the whole idea, hence 'shacket.'
terms.plateHint: A flat overshirt with the shirt-style buttons and collar labeled, plus a note on the heavier cloth and patch pockets.

terms.gloss: A fitted leather jacket that closes with an off-center diagonal zip.
terms.quickRead: A leather jacket with an off-center zip.
terms.closerRead: The diagonal, off-center zip, the wide snap-down lapels, the zippered pockets, and a waist belt are the biker signatures, all designed to close flat against the wind.
terms.plateHint: A flat leather jacket with the asymmetric zip, the snap lapels, and the waist belt labeled.

terms.gloss: A light, thin-padded jacket with diamond or channel quilting.
terms.quickRead: A light, padded jacket with a diamond-stitched pattern.
terms.closerRead: Diamond or channel quilting traps a thin layer of warmth without bulk; often collarless with a snap or zip front, it can be worn alone or zipped inside a heavier coat as a liner.
terms.plateHint: A flat quilted jacket with the diamond stitching pattern shown and the snap front and collarless neck labeled.

terms.gloss: An insulated jacket with sewn baffles holding lofted down or synthetic fill.
terms.quickRead: A puffy insulated jacket.
terms.closerRead: Horizontal sewn 'baffles' hold lofted down or synthetic fill, giving the pillowy segmented look; more fill and tighter baffles mean more warmth.
terms.plateHint: A flat puffer with the horizontal baffles labeled and a cutaway showing the lofted fill inside one channel.

terms.gloss: A low, clean court-style sneaker in leather or canvas.
terms.quickRead: A plain low sneaker.
terms.closerRead: A low, clean court shoe; the tell is the flat cup or vulcanized sole, a modest toe, and minimal branding, and the white-leather version has become a near-neutral everyday shoe.
terms.plateHint: A side-profile sneaker flat with the low collar, the slim sole, and the clean toe labeled.

terms.gloss: A sneaker built on an oversized, layered sole with a padded, paneled upper.
terms.quickRead: A big, cushioned running-style sneaker.
terms.closerRead: The exaggerated stacked sole and mixed-material paneling are the giveaway, deliberately bulky where a court sneaker is slim; the 'dad' name nods to its unhurried, comfort-first proportions.
terms.plateHint: A side-profile sneaker flat emphasizing the tall multi-layer midsole and paneled upper, next to a slim low-top for scale.

terms.gloss: A lace-up dress shoe with open lacing, where the lace flaps sit on top of the front.
terms.quickRead: A lace-up dress shoe.
terms.closerRead: The lace flaps sit on top of the shoe front and are stitched open at the bottom (open lacing); that is what makes it a derby, roomier and a touch less formal than a closed-laced oxford.
terms.plateHint: A side view of a lace-up shoe with the open-lacing flaps sitting on top of the vamp highlighted.

terms.gloss: A low, laceless slip-on shoe, often with a strap across the top.
terms.quickRead: A slip-on leather shoe.
terms.closerRead: No laces, you just step in; the strap across the top tells the type: a cut band with a slot is a penny loafer, a metal snaffle is a bit loafer, and fringe-with-strings is a tassel.
terms.plateHint: A side view of a slip-on shoe with the saddle strap across the vamp labeled, showing a penny-slot variant.

terms.gloss: A sleek ankle boot with elastic side panels and no laces.
terms.quickRead: A sleek ankle boot with no laces.
terms.closerRead: Elastic gore panels on each side let it pull on, and there is usually a fabric loop at the back heel to tug; clean, seamless, and lace-free is the whole look.
terms.plateHint: A side view of an ankle boot with the elastic side gore and the rear heel pull-tab labeled.

terms.gloss: A sturdy lace-up leather boot built for hard wear and resoling.
terms.quickRead: A rugged lace-up leather boot.
terms.closerRead: A cap or plain toe, half a dozen eyelets, and a stout welted lug or leather sole made to be resoled; the 'service boot' pattern comes straight from military and work heritage.
terms.plateHint: A side view of a lace-up boot with the toe cap, the eyelets, and the welted lug sole labeled.

terms.gloss: A low ankle boot with two or three eyelets, classically in unlined suede on a crepe sole.
terms.quickRead: A simple suede ankle boot with a couple of eyelets.
terms.closerRead: Just two or three lace eyelets on an unlined suede upper; a crepe (gum) sole makes it a 'desert boot' specifically, light and soft where a service boot is heavy.
terms.plateHint: A side view of a low ankle boot with the two-eyelet lacing and the pale crepe sole labeled.

terms.gloss: A simple canvas sneaker vulcanized onto a rubber sole.
terms.quickRead: A simple canvas sneaker.
terms.closerRead: A canvas upper vulcanized onto a rubber sole with a visible foxing stripe running around the edge; the low-tech gym-shoe build behind Chucks and classic skate shoes.
terms.plateHint: A side view of a canvas sneaker with the foxing stripe around the sole edge and the canvas upper labeled.

terms.gloss: A rugged, cushioned running shoe built for off-road use and adopted for everyday wear.
terms.quickRead: A rugged, cushioned running shoe.
terms.closerRead: An aggressive lugged outsole, a padded technical mesh upper, and often bright colorways; built for trails but widely worn as an everyday 'gorpcore' shoe.
terms.plateHint: A side view of a running shoe with the deep lugged outsole and the technical layered upper labeled.

terms.gloss: A dress shoe closed with one or two buckled straps instead of laces.
terms.quickRead: A dress shoe closed with a buckle instead of laces.
terms.closerRead: One or two straps cross the top and fasten with buckles, with no laces at all; the double-buckle version reads as a small statement against a plain lace-up.
terms.plateHint: A side view of a slip-on dress shoe with the crossing straps and buckles across the vamp labeled.
